measured_on.note: results are stale once `engine` differs from the shipped ENGINE_VERSION; release_preflight.py enforces this

title: Where a query's latency actually goes
why: A single end-to-end number blends three costs with different owners. Reporting only the blend invites a reader to re-run it on a different embedder and conclude the store is slow.
machine: Apple M4 Pro, macOS 26.5, 12 logical CPUs

corpus.query: an entity key, filtered to that entity, with as_of set

reading: The STORE costs 2.09 ms. That is the part nanomem owns.
The embedding round-trip costs 12.04 ms and is a property of the embedder you point it at, not of the store.
Query decomposition, on by default, cost 35.6 ms on this SHORT identifier-like query -- 3.4x end to end. It embeds sub-queries separately.
A 60-query sample over DISTINCT entities, so no single-entity cache warmth.

store_side_filtered_search_before_and_af.note: measured with the deterministic offline encoder so the store is isolated from the embedder

caveat: A caller that batches or caches query embeddings sees the 2.09 ms figure. A caller that embeds per query over HTTP does not, whatever store is underneath.
